text:
maria: Quick sync — we need a decision on the capacity-brokerage guardrails for Dedicated. AcmeHealth pilot requires deterministic 99th pct latency and a guaranteed burst window. My rough proposal: soft-reserve bands, a configurable spillover cap to shared lanes, explicit preemptibility tiers, and commit-window hedging. Need eng + SRE + sales sign-off by EOD Fri. PT: https://go/redwood/dedicated/brokerage-proposal

kevin: +1 on locking this down. main engineering concerns: eviction semantics and KV cache warmup cost when spilling over. Suggest policy flags: `preempt_tier`, `spillover_limit`, `eviction_notice_hours`, `commit_window_hours`. Example policy blob (for discussion):
```json
{
  "spillover_limit": 0.15,
  "preempt_tier": "shared",
  "eviction_notice_hours": 2,
  "commit_window_hours": 24
}
```
we can default to 15% spillover and tune per-customer.

alex: Observability + oncall notes: need tenant-labelled traces for 99th pct and a preemption counter metric (`dedicated.preempt.count`) so we can correlate errors. Also add a runbook for graceful eviction: how to fallback to hosted model or to a cached response. Preemptions during business hours will cause pager noise unless we buffer.

ben: AcmeHealth ask: cannot tolerate surprise preemption during their business hours (M-F 09:00-18:00 ET). They agreed to pay for a higher headroom if we provide a 2h eviction notice and explicit billing label for burst usage. They want documentation and an SLA addendum.

sophia: For roadmap gating, propose launch criteria:
- Pilot with 4 customers (incl. AcmeHealth) for 3 weeks with no >2% SLA violations on p99
- Observability: tenant traces + preempt metrics in Console
- Ops: runbook + eviction notice mechanism implemented
- Billing: per-burst meter and customer-acknowledged contract addendum
If those are met we can roll to GA behind a feature flag.

maria: Ownership & timeline suggestion: kevin -> implement policy flags + bench (ETA 2 sprints), alex -> observability/runbook (ETA 1 sprint), sophia -> gating & docs, ben -> customer contract/handshake. can folks confirm?

kevin: Confirm. i'll prototype the policy endpoint and a canary with `spillover_limit` control. I'll run a synthetic workload to measure KV cache refill cost and add a toggle for immediate vs. delayed spillover.

alex: Confirm. i'll add `dedicated.preempt.count`, `dedicated.spillover.rate`, and a tenant p99 dashboard. i'll draft runbook for graceful fallback.

ben: Confirm — i'll draft the SLA addendum and get AcmeHealth to sign the pilot terms.

opsbot: Doc created: /docs/dedicated/capacity-brokerage-guardrails.md (owned by sophia)

maria: OK — i'll consolidate action items and put a short milestone in the roadmap doc. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kevin: one more thought — default `spillover_limit` at 15% might be conservative; for some models 10% still protects p99 while saving cost. i'll surface numbers in the bench results.

sophia: noted. we'll treat the default as conservative and expose per-customer overrides behind the pilot flag.

maria: Great. Meeting scheduled if needed: Fri 16:00 PT to finalize if we haven't closed tasks.
